paper.title_en: Reconstructed traversable wormholes and lensing features in linear <math altimg="si9.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1247"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">L</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> gravity
paper.abstract_en: In this work, we investigate static and spherically symmetric traversable wormhole geometries in the linear <math altimg="si1.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1343"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">L</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mi>R</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mo><mi>β</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">L</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mo><mi>η</mi><mi>T</mi></mrow></math> gravity model. By adopting the Morris–Thorne metric with a finite redshift function <math altimg="si2.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1390"><mrow><mi>Φ</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mo><msub><mrow><mi>Φ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></math> and an anisotropic fluid satisfying a radially varying equation of state <math altimg="si3.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1441"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mi>ω</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>;</mo><mi>ω</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><msub><mrow><mi>ω</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mo><msub><mrow><mi>ω</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo></mrow></math> we reconstruct the shape function <math altimg="si520.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1523"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> from the modified field equations. The resulting reconstruction equation is a first-order linear differential equation, whose formal integral solution is obtained after imposing the throat condition <math altimg="si5.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1536"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><msub><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>. The flare-out condition, regularity of the reconstruction equation, and asymptotic flatness are used to identify an admissible parameter branch of the model. For representative parameter choices, the reconstructed solutions satisfy the required wormhole conditions. The radial null energy condition of the physical anisotropic matter sector is violated near the throat, as expected from the flare-out condition, while the tangential NEC remains non-negative over the representative numerical diagnostic domain. This indicates that the exoticity is mainly localized in the radial sector close to the throat. We also analyze the null geodesics and gravitational lensing properties of the reconstructed geometry. The off-throat circular null-orbit condition is governed by the redshift function and shows that no off-throat photon sphere exists for <math altimg="si6.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1563"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after"><</mo><msub><mrow><mi>Φ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after"><</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math>. However, in the two-sided wormhole extension, the throat itself can act as an unstable light ring. Therefore, the finite deflection angles obtained for photons with closest approach radius <math altimg="si430.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1582"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>∗</mo></mrow></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">></mo><msub><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> describe the weak-to-moderate lensing branch away from the throat-light-ring limit. The embedding diagram confirms the regular flare-out structure of the reconstructed spatial geometry. These results show that the linear <math altimg="si9.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1603"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">L</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> model admits reconstructed wormhole configurations with localized energy-condition violation and characteristic off-throat lensing features.
